Looking at the source, the `ordered` function has a bug: both branches of the `if` return `{"start" start "end" finish}` — the false branch should swap start and finish. This causes intervals with start > end to stay out of order, breaking merge logic.

Let me test my understanding, then produce the fix

args.program:
(defn ordered-fixed
  "Put one interval into ascending endpoint order."
  [interval]
  (let [start (get interval "start")
        finish (get interval "end")]
    (if (<= start finish)
      {"start" start "end" finish}
      {"start" finish "end" start})))  ;; FIX: swap when start > finish

(defn touches?
  [current next tolerance]
  (<= (get next "start")
      (+ (get current "end") tolerance)))

(defn extend
  [current next]
  {"start" (get current "start")
   "end" (max (get current "end") (get next "end"))})

(defn merge-ordered
  [intervals tolerance]
  (reduce
    (fn [merged interval]
      (if (empty? merged)
        [interval]
        (let [current (last merged)]
          (if (touches? current interval tolerance)
            (conj (vec (butlast merged)) (extend current interval))
            (conj merged interval)))))
    []
    intervals))

(defn merge-with-tolerance
  [input]
  (let [tolerance (get input "tolerance" 0)
        intervals (map ordered-fixed (get input "intervals" []))
        sorted (sort-by #(get % "start") intervals)]
    (return {"intervals" (merge-ordered sorted tolerance)})))
